text: Glioblastoma cells exploit glutamate via Ca²⁺-permeable AMPA receptors; Ca²⁺ influx phosphorylates Akt at Ser-473, driving proliferation and motility. Dominant-negative Akt blocked AMPA-receptor-accelerated proliferation/migration, while constitutively active Akt rescued apoptosis caused by converting receptors to Ca²⁺-impermeable via GluR2 cDNA. This glutamate–AMPA–Akt pathway may underlie anaplasia and invasive growth, offering a therapeutic target. In mast cells, Ca²⁺ oscillations accompanied by Ca²⁺ entry through store-operated CRAC channels triggered gene expression, whereas oscillations without entry did not; increased buffering prevented oscillations but not gene activation, indicating that local Ca²⁺ influx, not global oscillations, drives gene expression at physiological stimulation. During LTP, synaptic incorporation of GluR1-containing AMPA receptors is controlled by a PKC phosphorylation site on GluR1.
